coverage.assessment: The brandy, coal-lift and key chains hold. The cuts thin two motivations: why staying protects Rita, and what moves Tuppence's promise to sit up (F6, F8).
The locked door, the balcony and the boudoir are consistent. The discovery no longer shows Rita in the bed, or Tuppence crossing to the blinds and turning, before the cold hand (F2).
Speaker attributions are clear throughout. Julius's 'door open' argument is cut short, and the transitional 'lack of assurance' beat before Tuppence's outburst is gone (F7).
'The power of the money bribe could not fail' now reads as the narrator's flat claim, not Tuppence's post-meal comfort (F1).
There is no premature disclosure. Some of Sir James's ambivalent signals are thinned: the 'tone of those simple words' and the probing questions about Hall (F3, F4).
The broken speech and the hook survive. The relief-then-dread rhythm of the discovery is lost, and Julius's 'Bully' slang is thinned.
Suspicion stays split between the two men, but the neutral cue that Julius was 'some time' at the safe has been removed (F5).
All five dependencies are intact at both endpoints in the new drafts of 015, 026, 027 and 028.

strengths: The brandy sequence keeps every handler: washstand, tantalus, Julius to Sir James, Sir James forcing, Tuppence holding the glass. All of it stays neutral.
Rita's broken 'Don't--leave----', 'sleepy' and 'Mr.--Brown----' keep their dashes and ambiguity.
'If it is luck,' Julius's 'Plumb impossible' against Sir James's silence, and the 'Now-- _it was empty_' hook preserve the source's suspicion balance and chapter ending.
Continuity holds: the door is locked from outside, Tuppence uses her own key, and the balcony reaches only the boudoir.
summary: All five dependencies survive in both endpoints. The brandy chain, the locked door and key, the balcony limit, the safe pause and the closing hook are intact. No suspect is shown handling the chloral, and nothing is revealed early. The losses come mostly from the revision's extra compression. The bribe line has lost its anchor in Tuppence's point of view. The relief-then-dread timing of the discovery is gone. So is Tuppence's perception of Sir James's 'We must find out'. Julius's time at the safe is gone too. These are editorial repairs, not blockers.
